question: Should Feishu/Lark `thread=true` current-conversation subagent binding support plain non-topic group chats, and if so should it bind the whole group, the group plus sender, or another explicit conversation identity?
rationale: Current code intentionally limits binding adoption to DMs and topic-scoped groups; changing plain groups can affect session-state and message-delivery semantics for existing Feishu deployments.

options.title: Define explicit group binding contract
options.body: Choose group identity semantics, then update Feishu resolver, inbound route adoption, docs, and tests around that contract.

options.title: Keep DM/topic only
options.body: Document plain groups as unsupported for current-conversation binding and point persona workflows to static group routing or broader per-user-agent design.

options.title: Fold into broader policy work
options.body: Defer this issue to the generic channel threading policy or Feishu per-user-subagent design before changing behavior.

recommendation.title: Define explicit group binding contract
recommendation.body: Choose group identity semantics, then update Feishu resolver, inbound route adoption, docs, and tests around that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent core thread-binding refactor makes this the best available owner for the cross-channel policy decision.
